name: GitHub CLI 2.105.0
body:
## What's Changed

## Subscribe to GitHub Event Streams with `gh event` (preview)

The new `gh event` command set lets agents, integrations, and scripts wait for pull request changes instead of polling GitHub:

```shell
# Wait for a review event
gh event listen --resource https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER --event com.github.pull_request.review.submitted.v1 --timeout 30m

# Wait for a check suite completion event
gh event listen --resource https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/pull/NUMBER --event com.github.pull_request.check_suite.status.changed.v1 --jq .data.conclusion

# List active event subscriptions
gh event subscription list
```

By default, `gh event listen` exits after the first event. Use `--count` to wait for several events or `--follow` to keep listening. Events are printed as CloudEvent JSON objects, with `data.api_url` pointing to the resource that changed.

Supported events include submitted reviews, pull request state and head changes, merge conflicts, and completed check suites. The `subscription create`, `list`, `view`, and `delete` commands manage subscriptions directly.

> [!NOTE]
> GitHub Event Streams is in preview. [Join the wait list](https://gh.io/event-streams-signup), read the [announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-event-streams-is-now-in-preview), or see the [Event Streams documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/integrations/how-tos/using-github-event-streams).

## What's Changed

### ✨ Features

* Add a server-sent events reader and Event Subscriptions API client by @babakks in [#15071](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15071)
* Add `gh event listen` to wait for pull request events without polling by @babakks in [#15072](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15072)
* Add `gh event subscription list` by @babakks in [#15073](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15073)
* Add `gh event subscription create` by @babakks in [#15074](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15074)
* Add `gh event subscription view` by @babakks in [#15075](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15075)
* Add `gh event subscription delete` by @babakks in [#15076](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15076)
* Suggest `gh event listen` to agents using `gh pr` and `gh api` by @babakks in [#15077](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15077)
* Support check suite events and suggest them from `gh run view` and `gh run watch` by @babakks in [#15081](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15081)

### 🐛 Fixes

* fix(event listen): print each event without waiting for the next heartbeat by @babakks and @iancanderson in [#15079](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15079)
* fix(event listen): report deleted subscriptions clearly by @babakks in [#15080](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15080)
* fix(event): improve stream framing, `Retry-After` handling, evals, and regression coverage by @babakks in [#15083](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15083)

### 📚 Docs & Chores

* Make issue-triage formatting checks nonblocking by @BagToad in [#15052](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15052)
* Add event-driven agent evals, `gh` skill guidance, and preview documentation by @babakks in [#15078](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15078)

### :dependabot: Dependencies

* chore(deps): bump `golang.org/x/text` from 0.43.0 to 0.44.0 by @dependabot in [#15049](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15049)
* chore(deps): bump `golang.org/x/term` from 0.47.0 to 0.48.0 by @dependabot in [#15048](https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/15048)

name: v2.9.0
body:
## [2.9.0] - 2026-11-17

QMD adds document processors, metadata filtering, and remote model support.
This release also updates llama.cpp and hardens concurrent indexing and MCP
shutdown.

### Fixed

- Serialize trust-record mutations and atomically publish the trust file, so
  concurrent approvals and revocations do not overwrite each other.
- Share a crash-recoverable SQLite sidecar lock across CLI, SDK and direct
  embedding runs, preventing concurrent partial-vector cleanup from deleting
  another run's completed vectors.
- Hold the index's embed lock in `clearAllEmbeddings`, so a clear cannot drop
  the vector table under a running embed or resurrect vectors it just deleted.
- Keep SDK configuration sources separate per store. Coordinate LLM sessions,
  idle unloading and disposal so in-flight operations retain their resources.
- Wait for admitted SDK operations before closing their store, and reject
  reentrant closes instead of closing SQLite beneath active work.
- Bound MCP shutdown to a five-second grace period by default. On timeout,
  cancel requests and report failure without disposing resources still in use.
- Stream MCP event responses instead of buffering them indefinitely, and cancel
  requests when their clients disconnect.
- Serialize overlapping scans on one connection and make processor publication
  and embedding retry states explicit.
- Reconcile document changes made during CJK FTS shadow rebuilding before
  publishing, so concurrent writes remain searchable.
- Serialize YAML configuration mutations and publish them atomically, retaining
  concurrent edits and the permissions and targets of existing config files.
  Synchronize SQLite against the current locked config snapshot so an older
  opener cannot remove another process's newly added collection, and publish
  SDK collection and context changes before mirroring them, so a refused config
  write leaves no database-only edit or stale `config_hash`. A rename records
  the old→new pair before publishing, so an interrupted index move is finished
  by repeating the command and is never inferred from a name that merely exists;
  repeating a removal finishes it the same way. While that marker is live, a
  second rename or any change to either name is refused with
  `PendingRenameError` instead of destroying the only evidence, and an
  unreadable or malformed marker fails closed with `CorruptPendingRenameError`
  rather than being read as "no rename".
- Coordinate MCP daemon PID-file claims and stale recovery between current
  versions, preventing concurrent starters from displacing a live daemon.
- Avoid leaking Nix libc to host subprocesses, and use the build target instead
  of running `uname` to select the Darwin launcher mitigation.
- Expose the matching C++ runtime in the Linux Nix development shell so Bun can
  load the packaged llama.cpp backend.
- Correct the Python and Go grammar repair hints to use their pinned versions.
- Keep memory-regression coverage effective when Bun's SQLite does not track
  allocations for `hard_heap_limit`.

- Security: MCP stdio and HTTP startup now enforce project-local config trust
  before selecting models, ignoring all unapproved model URIs and options,
  including remote embedding credential environment variable names.

- `qmd doctor` selects vector sample identities before loading document bodies,
  avoiding excessive SQLite memory use on large indexes with duplicate paths.
  #978 (thanks @naveenspark)
- Vector diagnostics match passages by their saved character position, avoiding
  false mismatches when earlier chunks change the sequence numbering.
  #978 (thanks @naveenspark)

### Added

- Check bounded TLA+ models for lock, trust, indexing, processor, SDK and
  server lifecycles in CI, including intentional counterexample controls.

- Per-collection processors turn source files into stable-key Markdown index
  documents through explicit SDK callbacks or trusted argv commands. Bounded
  whole-source validation and SQL savepoints retain the last complete result on
  processing failures; source fingerprints skip unchanged work and preserve
  unchanged output vectors. Empty coverage and processor-mode markers prevent
  silent raw-input fallback after configuration removal. Commands are not an OS
  sandbox; see `docs/PROCESSORS.md` for trust, versioning and crash boundaries.
- Optional TypeSafe System One reranking through `models.rerank: typesafe:<model>`
  and copied per-store `rerankOptions` (revision and credential variable name).
  Independent per-document scores use bounded two-worker HTTP, caller/session
  cancellation and revision-specific cache identities, without a local reranker.
  Public SDK search accepts a signal; duplicate-file chunks cache by result index.
  Status/doctor do not probe the remote service; pull skips its download.
  Local models and cache keys are unchanged. Adapted from #1014
  (thanks @caseymanos).
- Explicit OpenAI-compatible remote embeddings through `models.embed` API-base
  URIs (`http[s]://host/v1#model-id`), with bounded requests/responses,
  caller/session cancellation and opt-in credential environment variable names.
  SDK and CLI indexing need no local embedding model or tokenizer. Remote space
  identities pin the endpoint, model, dimensions, revision and input format;
  vector search enforces remote space boundaries in scope and reads matches
  from one post-request SQLite snapshot. Remote queries require exact model/
  fingerprint matches; local queries refuse remote rows without changing existing
  local-to-local or legacy-fingerprint behavior. Local GGUF defaults are unchanged.
  Adapted from #761 (thanks @epruseal).
- Added Oxlint lint fence.
- Document metadata and metadata filtering. Markdown documents can opt into typed metadata through a namespaced frontmatter block (`qmd.metadata` with strings, numbers, booleans, or flat homogeneous arrays), and every search surface — CLI `search`/`vsearch`/`query` via `--filter <json>`, the SDK's `filter` option on `search()`/`searchLex()`/`searchVector()`, the MCP `query` tool, and HTTP `POST /query` and `/search` — accepts one shared recursive filter AST discriminated by `operator`: `and`/`or`/`not` logical groups, `eq`/`ne`/`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` comparisons, `in`/`nin`/`all` membership, `contains`/`prefix`/`suffix` text matching, `type` for the stored type of a key's values, and `exists` presence, with an optional `caseInsensitive` flag on any condition whose value is a string (ASCII folding). Every returned result satisfies the filter (applied before RRF fusion and reranking); like collection filtering, highly selective filters remain best-effort for top-K completeness. Frontmatter stays ordinary searchable content — no chunking, embedding, snippet, or line-number changes — and documents without `qmd.metadata` behave exactly as before. JSON/SDK/MCP/HTTP results now include each document's indexed metadata, and `qmd status` reports how many documents still need metadata extraction (a normal `qmd update` backfills existing indexes).
- Metadata discovery. Filtering is only useful when the caller knows what to filter on, so every surface now reports the metadata keys, types, and value counts already in the index — read from the existing metadata tables, with no re-indexing. The CLI adds `qmd collection metadata [name...]` with `--filter <json>` to count only documents matching a filter (same AST as search) and `--match <json>` to select which metadata entries are reported (the same AST evaluated per entry, where a condition's `field` is the entry's `key` or `value`, so one grammar covers a single key, a family of keys, reverse lookup of a value, typed thresholds, and any `and`/`or`/`not` composition), plus `--key-limit`/`--key-offset`/`--all-keys` and `--value-limit`/`--value-offset`/`--all-values` to page both windows, and `--sort count|value` and `--min-count <n>` to order and trim values. Every windowed list reports its exact remainder, counts are documents rather than values, numbers report min/median/max, keys whose documents disagree on type are split per type with their own counts, and with `--filter` every coverage count is measured against the documents the filter admits. `qmd collection list` names each collection's top keys, `qmd collection show` details them with a value preview, and `qmd status` summarizes coverage. The SDK adds `listMetadata(options)` (the same options, spelled `keyLimit`, `valueLimit`, and so on, with `MetadataOptionError` for a value outside its domain and `MetadataBindingBudgetError` for a filter and match that together bind too many SQL parameters), the MCP server adds a `metadata` tool and lists each collection's most covered keys in `status`, and the HTTP server adds `POST /metadata`. `MetadataFilter` and `MetadataMatch` are both `MetadataPredicate<Condition>`, one recursive grammar over the conditions a document or a metadata entry admits.

### Fixed

- Filtered vector search binds candidate IDs as one JSON list, so a parser-valid metadata filter cannot exhaust Node's SQL variable limit during document lookup. Applies to both exact scans and the capped global fallback.
- Collection- and metadata-scoped BM25 search (`qmd search -c`, the lex leg of
  `qmd query`, MCP, SDK `searchLex`) no longer returns false-empty or
  incomplete results when stronger matches outside the scope fill the old
  `limit * 10` candidate window (#922). The scope is now applied to the full
  FTS5 match set, materialized once, so `search -c <collection>` is exact for
  common terms; unscoped search keeps its early-terminating plan. A search over
  several collections, such as the default ones, runs one keyword query instead
  of one per collection, which made keyword search about 12x faster over 13
  collections (thanks @brettdavies). Builds on the approach in #918 (thanks
  @fxstein). #953 (thanks @Mr-Beasley)

- `qmd update` no longer deactivates every document in a collection whose root
  folder is missing, for example an unmounted drive or an offline network share.
  The folder globbed to an empty list, which read as "every file was deleted",
  so search went empty and a `qmd cleanup` before the drive came back deleted
  the rows for good. The collection is now reported as not found and its index
  is left unchanged. Permission and I/O errors still fail with their original
  cause (#989). #990 (thanks @ParkerRex)
- Embedding generation and legacy fingerprint adoption now tokenize documents
  with the store-selected embedding model instead of the global default. This
  keeps chunk boundaries aligned with the model that creates and verifies the
  stored vectors without initializing an unrelated provider.
- `qmd doctor` no longer stalls or fills the temp directory on large indexes
  when checking legacy (empty-fingerprint) embeddings. The adoption sample
  query joined `content` and grouped by the document body, so SQLite
  materialized the full body once per legacy chunk and per active path before
  `LIMIT 1` discarded it, the same pattern as the doctor vector-sample check
  (#978). It now picks the sample row through indexes and loads only that
  row's body; the sampled chunk is unchanged (#994). #995 (thanks @mjaverto)

### Changed

- Update `node-llama-cpp` 3.20.0 → 3.22.3 (llama.cpp v0.9.0), MCP server
  2.0.0 → 2.4.0, `web-tree-sitter` 0.26.12 → 0.27.2, and other compatible
  runtime and development dependencies. Refresh Bun, pnpm and Nix dependency
  metadata; Vitest stays on 3 and TypeScript on 5 for compatibility.

- The MCP server caches its instructions per store for up to 60 seconds instead
  of rebuilding them, with a full index-status scan, for every HTTP request.
  Concurrent requests share one build and a failed build is not cached; index
  changes from other processes show up in the instructions within a minute.
  #815 (thanks @fxstein)
- Avoid a redundant runtime process on packaged CLI calls where the launcher is
  already running under its selected Node or Bun runtime. #923 (thanks @ilepn)
- `qmd update` no longer reads files whose modification time and size match
  the last pass (tracked in a new `file_sync_state` table), so re-indexing an
  unchanged collection takes seconds. A cached entry counts only while its
  document is still active at that path with that content, so a collection
  removed and added back is re-indexed, while a renamed one keeps its entries;
  files with missing or outdated metadata are still re-extracted. `qmd update`
  and `qmd collection add` skip files over 10 MB with `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, and
  `qmd update` deactivates a previously indexed file that becomes empty or is
  over 10 MB, including one indexed by an earlier release. #962 (thanks
  @rikvanriel)
- Search results carry at most the first 262,144 characters of each document
  body (`qmd search --full`, MCP results, keyword and vector hits), which
  bounds memory on indexes with very large documents. A match past that point
  is still found, but its snippet, and the passage the reranker scores, come
  from the start of the document. #962 (thanks @rikvanriel)
- `qmd update` and `qmd collection add` write a collection scan in short
  transactions instead of committing every row on its own, so a first index
  of 20,000 files takes about 5 s instead of about 3 minutes. #1021 (thanks
  @brettdavies)

- `qmd query` and `qmd vsearch` now drop repeated query expansions before
  searching. The expansion model can repeat a line, and the cache kept every
  copy: one reported query ran 23 expansions where 9 were distinct, and each
  copy ran its own search. Cached expansions are deduplicated when read, so
  existing caches need no rebuild. Repeated lex lines used to count more than
  once in the rank fusion, so result order can shift slightly. (#921)
  #1000 (thanks @ParkerRex)
- Structured searches over several collections (`qmd query` with
  `lex:`/`vec:`/`hyde:` lines, the MCP `query` tool, SDK `queries`) run one
  search per line over the whole collection list, a keyword search for a
  `lex:` line and a vector search for a `vec:` or `hyde:` line, and fuse one
  ranked list per search. Rankings no longer depend on the order the
  collections are named. #946 (thanks @shalom-t), #1009 (thanks @xidus90)

### Changed

- The vector index is partitioned by collection. Each embedded chunk is
  stored once per collection that holds it, under an integer collection id,
  so a collection-scoped `qmd query` or `qmd vsearch` scans only that
  collection's vectors instead of pre-filtering the whole index, and a small
  collection is never crowded out of the results by a large one. The first
  command after upgrading converts the index in place and prints its
  progress; the conversion resumes from where it stopped if interrupted, two
  commands started at once share it, and a VACUUM at the end reclaims the
  space of the old table. `qmd collection rename` no longer touches vectors,
  `qmd update` removes, as it finishes, the vectors of content that no
  indexed document holds any more (content that comes back later is embedded
  again), and `qmd update` and `qmd embed` copy an already-embedded document
  into a collection that gains it instead of embedding it again. A
  metadata-filtered vector search returns the nearest documents the filter
  admits however many chunks it admits, and a vector search fills its limit
  even when one long document holds all of the nearest chunks. Downgrading
  to an older qmd afterwards needs `qmd embed -f`, and a `qmd mcp` server
  started before the upgrade must be restarted. #983 (thanks @brettdavies)

### Changed

- `qmd cleanup` repacks the vector table when fewer than 90% of its chunk
  reads hold live rows. vec0 fills the first free slot of its newest chunk
  and reclaims a chunk only once it is empty, so re-embeds and orphan removal
  leave holes in older chunks that every brute-force scan still reads; a
  794k-vector index at 36% occupancy scanned twice as slowly as a packed copy
  of the same rows. The repack moves the live rows of each mostly-empty chunk
  to the tail, one chunk per short transaction, so it never holds the write
  lock for long and an interrupted run leaves a consistent table. The cleanup
  output and `qmd cleanup --dry-run` report the chunk counts.
  #937 (thanks @brettdavies)

name: Sub2API 0.2.23
body:
> AI API Gateway Platform - 将 AI 订阅配额分发和管理

接入 GPT-6.2 Sol 和 Astra，支持 Ultra Fast 档位；修正多条协议转换链路上的缓存写入用量和计费。

## 新增功能

- 支持 GPT-6.2 Sol / Astra 模型：价格与官方一致；上下文超过 272K 时按长上下文计费；Fast 档 2 倍价；Ultra Fast 档在 2027-03-01 00:00（太平洋时间）前是 3 倍促销价，之后自动切为 6 倍
- GPT-6.2 Ultra Fast 按订阅套餐放行：Pro 200 只开放 Sol，Pro 500 开放 Sol 和 Astra
- 渠道定价新增「Ultra Fast 倍率」，可按渠道覆盖。不填时沿用模型自带倍率，只影响 Ultra Fast 档

## 优化改进

- OpenAI 流式请求在首次输出前空闲超时，现在会切换账号重试，不再直接报错给客户端。最多切换 1 次，避免一个卡住的请求把超时惩罚扩散到整个账号池
- 流式空闲计时改为每收到上游数据就重置，避免持续出数据的长流被误判超时
- 原生 Chat Completions 流式透传减少 flush 次数，降低网关 CPU 占用
- DeepSeek reasoning 占位和 Ollama Cloud reasoning 回填改为一次改写请求体，大幅降低长对话请求的 CPU 和内存开销

## Bug 修复

- 修复 Anthropic ↔ OpenAI Responses / Chat Completions 互转时丢失缓存写入 TTL（5m/1h）明细的问题
- 修复缓存写入明细之和小于总量时少计费的问题，差额现在按 5m 价格补计
- 修复 OpenAI 网关走 Anthropic 原生路径时 1h 缓存写入按 5m 价格计费的问题，现在按 1h 价格计费
- 修复流式过程中只更新缓存字段时，prompt 总量和缓存写入总量被覆盖或算错的问题



---

## 📥 Installation

**Docker:**
```bash
# Docker Hub
docker pull weishaw/sub2api:0.2.23

# GitHub Container Registry
docker pull ghcr.io/wei-shaw/sub2api:0.2.23
```

**One-line install (Linux):**
```bash
curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/main/deploy/install.sh | sudo bash
```

**Manual download:**
Download the appropriate archive for your platform from the assets below.

## 📚 Documentation

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api)
- [Installation Guide](https://github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/blob/main/deploy/README.md)

name: @openviking/react 0.1.14
body:
## en-US

### Minor Changes

- 128b63d: AgentConnect accepts `isEnterprise` to show English or Chinese team onboarding instructions for agents supported by the official installer, preserving API key masking and copying. Existing instructions remain the default.

- 196fad5: Add OpenViking CLI session, file download, and OVPack commands to Console. Local inputs use the browser file picker. Administrator-only backup and restore require opting in through `commandOptions.allowAdminCommands`.

  With `--read-content`, Console search results display multiline file content and fall back to the abstract when content is unavailable or blank. Search result items support an optional `content` field for the multiline body.

- 81c42ac: Align the Console's built-in command options with the Volcengine terminal, including filesystem limits, search filters, ACL JSON, inline writes, resource import options, and task filters. Show the canonical names, aliases, and defaults in command help. `tree` now requires a directory URI, for example `ov tree viking://resources -L 2`.

- d510934: FileBrowser can show test materials, group source trajectories by update, and display trajectory documents and source messages when the host supplies the corresponding loaders.

- a8d37f3: Show timestamped transcripts and extracted frames in FileBrowser for processed video segments. Select a transcript entry to seek the video, or open an extracted frame at full size.

- b90eb2e: Show Create Wiki and Scheduled Report shortcuts in managed VikingBot. Use the toolbar @ or type @ in the draft to browse and search for files or directories to include with a message.

  After switching languages, select another shortcut to replace the previous preset draft.

### Patch Changes

- 0019eb7: Keep the active video transcript entry highlighted and in view during playback. Show extracted frame filenames, keep thumbnails stable when resizing the preview, and expand the video and transcript together while preserving playback.

- b62b243: The command console accepts Han characters in compile configuration names, up to 32 characters in total. ASCII-only names allow up to 64 characters.

- a961625: Allow Console hosts to control selected directory references while keeping the built-in picker and search. Reset the selection when switching or starting a conversation. Chat adapters can acknowledge accepted input before the reply arrives so a submitted clarification card can close promptly.

- d510934: FileBrowser shows the appropriate empty state when a directory has no L0 or L1 summary.

- 1c25783: Align the version history and copy icons in the FileBrowser editor with the console. Hide the dashboard tab during editing, show a folder-specific empty message, and label the shared resources root.

- 84e5f15: Keep retrieval mode selection beside the FileBrowser search field, including when there are no matches. Switching modes retains the query and compatible filters.

- 3e229d1: Prevent the copy-path tooltip from opening after a mouse-driven rollback when focus moves to the copy button. The tooltip still opens on hover or keyboard focus.

- b90eb2e: Make selected text stand out in the file editor, including on Wiki conflict lines.

- 85b3666: Hide in-progress resource import notifications in Console. Import progress stays visible in the command result, and Console still shows completion and failure notifications.

- 85b3666: Reveal the first conflict when opening the Wiki editor.

- 85b3666: Align the VikingBot reference picker with the file tree's root order.

- 85b3666: Close a submitted clarification when VikingBot resumes.

- b90eb2e: Enable the Load more and Retry buttons in the VikingBot reference picker so users can continue browsing directory pages and recover from listing errors.

- 13282ba: Show Rename and Delete in a per-session menu in VikingBot history.

- 85b3666: Keep the VikingBot history popover at a stable height during refresh, and show a centered diamond loader when switching conversations. Add session rename and delete actions when the session service supports them.

  Dismiss pending rename and delete confirmations when the session account or service changes. Standalone VikingBot hosts can provide `sessions.scopeKey` to identify their session scope.

- b90eb2e: Show a progress notification while FileBrowser saves Wiki changes, including conflict resolutions.

- 1c25783: Highlight unresolved Wiki conflicts in the FileBrowser editor and show their explanations on hover. Conflict metadata stays out of the draft.

- 6e8578d: Show the original Wiki conflict trailer in green at the end of the editor. The trailer is read-only, and saving still submits the editable body.

- a86d3a4: Align Markdown and YAML syntax colors and the Wiki conflict tooltip with the console editor. Load YAML front matter highlighting regardless of when the Markdown grammar is registered.

- b90eb2e: Label versions created by a Wiki rollback and show a confirmation after restoring a version or selecting identical content.

## zh-CN

### 功能更新

- 128b63d: AgentConnect 新增 `isEnterprise`，为支持官方安装器的 Agent 展示中英文团队接入文案，复用 API Key 脱敏和复制逻辑。默认继续使用原有文案。

- 196fad5: Console 新增 OpenViking CLI 会话、文件下载和 OVPack 命令。本地输入通过浏览器文件选择器提供。管理员备份和恢复需要通过 `commandOptions.allowAdminCommands` 显式启用。

  Console 检索命令使用 `--read-content` 时展示多行正文，正文不可读或为空白时回退到摘要。检索结果项支持通过可选的 `content` 字段提供多行正文。

- 81c42ac: 对齐 Console 内置命令与火山引擎终端的参数，包括文件系统限制、检索过滤、ACL JSON、正文写入、资源导入和任务筛选。在命令帮助中展示规范参数名、别名和默认值。`tree` 现在需要传入目录 URI，例如 `ov tree viking://resources -L 2`。

- d510934: 宿主提供相应的数据源后，文件浏览区块可分页展示测试素材，按经验更新分组展示来源轨迹，并在详情中查看轨迹正文和来源消息。

- a8d37f3: FileBrowser 支持展示已解析视频切片的带时间戳转录文稿和抽帧图片。点击文稿可跳转到对应播放位置，点击抽帧可放大图片。

- b90eb2e: 内置 VikingBot 新增「创建 Wiki」和「定时日报」快捷入口；可点击工具栏的 @ 或在输入框键入 @ 浏览和搜索文件或目录，并随消息发送引用。

  切换语言后，点击快捷入口仍可替换之前填入的预设草稿。

### 修复与改进

- 0019eb7: 播放视频时高亮当前转录文稿并自动滚动。显示抽帧文件名，拖动预览分栏时保持缩略图尺寸稳定，并支持在弹窗中同步查看视频和文稿，保留播放进度。

- b62b243: 命令台支持使用汉字创建和运行编译配置，含汉字的名称总长最多 32 个字符，纯 ASCII 名称最多 64 个字符。

- a961625: 允许宿主控制 Console 的目录引用选中项，同时保留内置目录树和搜索。切换或新建会话时清空引用。对话适配器可以在回复到达前确认输入已送达，让已提交的澄清卡及时关闭。

- d510934: 文件浏览区块对未生成摘要的目录显示对应的 L0 和 L1 空态。

- 1c25783: 对齐文件浏览区块编辑态的版本历史和复制图标，编辑时隐藏看板页签。展开空文件夹时显示专用提示，并为顶层资源目录添加共享标签。

- 84e5f15: 文件浏览器在搜索框旁常驻检索方式选择器，无匹配结果时也可以切换。切换时保留输入词和新模式支持的筛选。

- 3e229d1: 修复鼠标确认回滚后，焦点落到复制路径按钮时误弹提示的问题。悬停和键盘聚焦仍会显示提示。

- b90eb2e: 调整文件编辑器的文字选区颜色，使选区在 Wiki 冲突行上也清楚可见。

- 85b3666: 隐藏 Console 中进行中的资源导入通知。命令结果仍显示导入进度，Console 仍会显示任务完成和失败通知。

- 85b3666: 打开 Wiki 编辑器时定位首个冲突。

- 85b3666: 统一 VikingBot 引用选择器与文件树的根目录顺序。

- 85b3666: VikingBot 继续运行后关闭已提交的澄清弹窗。

- b90eb2e: 修复 VikingBot 引用选择器的「加载更多」和「重试」按钮，支持继续浏览目录分页并在目录加载失败后重试。

- 13282ba: VikingBot 历史会话将重命名和删除收拢到每行的更多操作菜单。

- 85b3666: 刷新时保持 VikingBot 历史会话弹层高度稳定，切换会话时居中显示菱形加载动画。会话服务支持相应操作时，提供会话改名和删除入口。

  切换会话账号或服务时关闭已打开的重命名和删除确认框。独立使用 VikingBot 时，宿主可通过 `sessions.scopeKey` 标识会话作用域。

- b90eb2e: FileBrowser 保存 Wiki 改动时显示进度通知，包括冲突解决后的保存。

- 1c25783: 在文件浏览区块的编辑器中高亮未解决的 Wiki 冲突，悬停时显示冲突说明。冲突元数据仍与草稿正文分离。

- 6e8578d: 在 Wiki 编辑器末尾以绿色显示原始冲突尾注。尾注只读，保存继续提交可编辑正文。

- a86d3a4: 将 Markdown、YAML 语法配色及 Wiki 冲突气泡与控制台编辑器对齐。Markdown 语法提前注册时也能高亮 YAML 文件头。

name: v16.0.0
body:
## My Work puts what needs you first

My Work, the page that shows what your agents are doing, was rebuilt from a full UI review (#6210, #6304). What needs you sits at the top, long lists fold, and every page works on a phone, by keyboard and with a screen reader.

- **What needs you comes first.** On the home page the first request waiting on you is at the top, with the one orange button on the screen. Requests are one-line rows; Idle and Shipped fold to one row each, with their counts.
- **Shorter pages.** On a real install: home is about 2,600px tall instead of 5,138; the List opens with 5 rows instead of 195; My Rules is about 4,400px instead of over 17,000.
- **Reply where you read.** A request's drawer puts the reply box right under its progress line, in every state. While a reply is on its way, "Reply here" waits, so a message can never go to a second conversation as a second paid turn.
- **A focus area's page** reads top to bottom: what needs you, the asks not started yet, then the board. A failed save says which change failed and offers Try again on that screen only. Past focus shows the day an area was marked done.
- **My Rules: one rule to decide at a time**, with one orange Approve. On a phone, swipe to decide.
- **Fits a phone.** Every page is 390px wide on a 390px phone, with a bottom bar for My Work, Focus and My Rules.
- **Keyboard and screen readers.** Every control has a name; tooltips open from Tab; focus comes back to where you were after a dialog, the drawer, Dismiss or Try again; controls are 44px on touch.
- **Theme before load.** Your light or dark choice is drawn before the first frame, loading and error screens included.
- **Plain errors.** A failure is one sentence in your language, with the raw reason folded under Details. Nothing retries by itself.
- **Your language and clock.** Times show in your language from the recorded time (French reads a 24-hour clock), and a day from another year shows its year. New strings are translated into French, Korean, Turkish and Chinese; corrections from native speakers are welcome.
- **Less motion.** A live update moves at most two things, and nothing moves with reduced motion on.

## Observation TV is removed

- **The TV page and its read-only remote access are gone** from the open-source worker (#6295): `/tv`, `tv.html` and the `CLAUDE_MEM_TV_TOKEN` setting. The classic viewer and My Work are unchanged.
- **If you watched TV from another machine:** set `CLAUDE_MEM_LOCAL_API_TOKEN`, which protects network access now, and delete `CLAUDE_MEM_TV_TOKEN`. Until you do, a worker that still finds the TV token with a non-loopback `CLAUDE_MEM_WORKER_HOST` and no local API token binds to `127.0.0.1` (`::1` for an IPv6 host) and logs a `SECURITY` error, so the full API is never open to the network without a token.
- Framing protection now covers every page the worker serves.

## Already shipped in 15.20.0 and 15.21.0

The rest of the same review reached you in 15.20.0:

- **Setup:** a step bar, Back on every screen, plain errors, and Stop import (#6233).
- **Classic viewer:** one header row, a searchable project picker, "Find in this session", and no React error 185 at the end of a long timeline (#6229).
- **Import from Mem0 and Supermemory:** acceptance fixes (#6206).
- **Fixes:** Codex Desktop sessions are read live on macOS (#6285, thanks @MaxWang007), and the worker starts when `settings.json` is not valid JSON (#6259).

15.21.0 followed: Code Mode starts with claude-mem enabled (#6278), auto-clear resumes with a continuation prompt (#6294), Hermes Desktop and GitHub Copilot in VS Code connect over MCP (#6284, #6286), and setup finishes when your prompt history is too large for one upload (#6280).

Full notes: [15.20.0](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/releases/tag/v15.20.0) and [15.21.0](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/releases/tag/v15.21.0).

## Also new

- **The SessionStart banner is a card in Claude Code terminals** (#6274). On Claude Code 2.1.326 or later, the Rules + Tools line, "Previously" and the timeline are drawn as one framed card. A session mirrored to the Claude app shows one line instead of the hook's name in front of every line of the banner.

## Fixes

- **The worker keeps answering while it works through a backlog.** Health checks, hooks and the viewer no longer wait behind:
  - a hook spool backlog: the drain reads files in parallel batches of 64 (#6260, thanks @Zhong-fan) and removes and claims them without blocking (#6296, from #6254 by @Afloat16); reported in #6247 by @soarkit;
  - the project list at worker start, which read every row and now reads the project indexes (#6270; reported in #6246 by @soarkit);
  - the Claude CLI check that corpus prime and query run on a cache miss (#6256, thanks @Afloat16; reported in #6250 by @soarkit);
  - Chroma sync's checkpoint, which was rewritten for every row (about 28 MB of writes for 2,000 rows) and is now written once per 250 ms (#6204, thanks @Zhong-fan; reported in #6203 by @soarkit).
- **Folder CLAUDE.md files:** updates fetch up to 8 folders at a time instead of one by one (#6264; reported in #6248 by @soarkit), `claude-mem generate` reads a project's observations once instead of once per folder (#6265; reported in #6249 by @soarkit), and a failed folder update is logged with its folder and tried again by the next observation for that folder (#6208, thanks @0xABCD01).
- **Long Bash output keeps its end** (#6292; reported in #6282 by @micronox). When Claude Code cut an output over about 30,000 characters and saved the full text to a file, the memory came from the start only, so the last lines (test summaries, final errors) were lost. claude-mem now reads the end from that file.
- **Native memory notes:** a note with `type:` at the top of its frontmatter keeps its category (#6244), and a note's project is found when the transcript's first prompt is long (#6272), thanks @Afloat16.
- **Recent sessions include adopted worktrees** (#6268, thanks @Afloat16). After a worktree was merged into its parent, OpenClaw's `claude-mem-recent` showed no previous sessions.
- **Search:** Chinese and Japanese terms inside longer unspaced words are found in corpus evidence (#6213, thanks @liuyinchu). `smart_outline`, `smart_search` and `smart_unfold` find JavaScript functions defined by assignment, such as `exports.read = function …` (#6245), and each Java method overload unfolds on its own (#6257), thanks @Afloat16.
- **Quieter error reports:** a context read that passes the 120-second reader deadline names the slow read and logs a warning, not an error (#6255), and on Windows a spool entry that Windows keeps locked gets one warning instead of an error report on every drain (#6269).
- **Two failures that were dropped are logged now** (#6302): auto-clear says so in the transcript when it could not hand Claude its request to save the work state, and the server logs why `/v1/info` could not read the vector search status.
- **Turkish:** clearer My Work wording and an up-to-date Turkish README (#6287, thanks @alkank).

## For contributors

- The commit-message test that needs bash 4 is skipped on macOS's bash 3.2, and still runs on Linux CI (#6297).

name: v15.21.0
body:
## claude-mem no longer turns off Claude Code's Code Mode

- **Code Mode starts with claude-mem enabled** (#6278, thanks @naive000; reported in #6209 by @nasif-naseef). Code Mode (experimental, Claude Code 2.1.323 and later) refuses to start when a plugin's hooks module hooks `tool.call`. claude-mem's auto-clear mod did, so Code Mode was off for everyone with claude-mem enabled, even with auto-clear off. The mod now reads tool results through `session.append` instead. Auto-clear still works on every Claude Code version that runs mods (2.1.287 and later).

## Auto-clear picks up where it left off

Auto-clear is still off unless you set `CLAUDE_MEM_AUTO_CLEAR_ENABLED` to `true`. When it is on:

- **It resumes with a continuation prompt instead of the bare word "continue"** (#6294). Before clearing, Claude saves its work state one last time, naming the list it is working from, the task it just finished and the overall goal. After `/clear`, auto-clear sends: `You are working on "<list>" and recently completed "<task>". Pick back up on our overarching goal "<goal>" from where you left off.` If that save left any of the three out, it sends "continue" as before and logs why.
- **It starts at 40% of the context window instead of 33%** (#6294). A `CLAUDE_MEM_AUTO_CLEAR_PERCENT` you set in `settings.json` or the environment still wins.

## New ways to connect

- **Hermes Desktop, search and save over MCP** (#6284, thanks @krishnadobhal; part of #5940). `claude-mem hermes install --mcp-only --project-cwd <absolute-directory>` adds claude-mem as an MCP server for Hermes One and Hermes Desktop without making it the memory provider. You get search and save when you ask for them; nothing is captured or injected on its own. `claude-mem hermes uninstall` removes only what it wrote and restores `config.yaml` byte for byte.
- **GitHub Copilot in VS Code** (#6286, thanks @krishnadobhal; part of #5895). `npx claude-mem install --ide copilot-vscode` writes the MCP entry that VS Code's Copilot agent reads (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, the same file Copilot CLI uses). The entry now includes `"tools": ["*"]`. Without it, VS Code connected to claude-mem but never offered its tools to the model. No automatic capture yet.
- **ModelGo preset** (#6277, thanks @lichloe1116-gif of the ModelGo team). The OpenAI-compatible provider has a `modelgo` preset for `https://api.modelgo.ai/v1`. It sets no default model, so pick one your key can use.

## Also new

- **Work-state write checks** (#6217, thanks @vieGPT). You can make `work_state_write` run a local check command before it writes to lists you choose, set in `~/.claude-mem/work-state-write-guard.json`. A refused write returns HTTP 409 and nothing is saved. With no file, nothing changes.
- **`CLAUDE_MEM_API_AGENT_EXTRA_BODY`** (#6225, thanks @Moep90; #6223). A JSON object added to every request the api agent sends (the My Work refresh and the corpus agent with `api`). For a Qwen model on vLLM, `{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}` turns reasoning off. Fields such as `model`, `messages` and `max_tokens` are dropped with a warning, and it is never sent to the cmem.ai gateway.

## My Work refresh

- **Slow answers from your own model no longer fail at about 5 minutes** (#6224, thanks @Moep90; #6222). Bun's fetch gave up on a connection that had been quiet for 5 minutes, before the api agent's 10-minute request limit applied. Now that limit is the only one.
- **Endpoints that want `max_completion_tokens` work** (#6242). When an endpoint refuses `max_tokens`, the api agent sends the request once more with `max_completion_tokens`, instead of failing every call with HTTP 400.
- **A refresh no longer stalls on an answer that was refused twice** (#6212, thanks @Moep90). On the one retry for grouping, focus or review, the parts that fail the checks are dropped and the rest is saved. Before, the same batch failed on every run.
- **The build story is written in parts** (#6279, thanks @0xABCD01; reported in #6226 by @Moep90). The story step sent every changed review in one question. That question grew past the model's context window, and every refresh after that failed. It now sends parts that fit the same question budget the other steps use.
- Long conversations are grouped by their latest requests, not their first ten (#6243, thanks @Afloat16).
- Commits made with `git commit --message` or `--message=` are recognized (#6236, thanks @Afloat16).
- A commit gets a GitHub link only when the evidence names one repository (#6237, thanks @Afloat16).
- While My Rules waits for an agent, it links the instructions for setting up an API refresh (#6214, thanks @liuyinchu).

## Setup, import and export

- **Setup finishes when your prompt history is large** (#6280, thanks @0xABCD01; #6266; reported in #6227 by @deserteaglemj). Setup stopped at 99% on "Finding your recent work" when the recent prompts were over the 2 MiB hosted upload limit, and every retry failed the same way. It now finishes setup on your machine and says so. The consent step also shows "Too much for one upload. Untick a tool or skip the scan." and turns off the upload button until the selection fits.
- **Large exports import** (#6261, thanks @Afloat16). A file over the worker's 5 MiB request limit was refused (HTTP 413) before anything was saved. Large files are now sent in parts, sessions first, with their full content.
- Imported observations are found by deduplication the same way live ones are, when `CLAUDE_MEM_DEDUP_ENABLED` is on (#6263, thanks @Afloat16).
- `claude-mem import --dry-run` no longer stops on a bad worker setting, since a preview never calls the worker (#6215, thanks @liuyinchu).
- Conversations Codex Desktop imported from another agent are no longer counted as prompts typed in Codex (#6219, thanks @rigel905; #6218).
- Exporting to `/dev/stdout`, `/dev/stderr`, a symlink to either, or a FIFO writes clean JSON there, and progress lines and warnings go to the other stream (#6288, from #6258 by @Afloat16).

## Fixes

- **Windows: Claude Code loads RULES-AND-TOOLS.md again** (#6234, thanks @QuantScorpus). claude-mem wrote its `@` import lines with backslashes. Claude Code skips those without a word, and claude-mem then also left out its other copy of the instructions, so neither reached the model. The lines now use forward slashes. An `@` import shown inside a fenced code example no longer counts as the real one (#6293, from #6241 by @Afloat16).
- **`claude-mem start` runs the installed worker** (#6235, thanks @ZedingZhang; reported in #6228 by @ExactDoug), not the copy an old shell alias points at, which can be missing its dependencies.
- **Backups keep the new snapshot after the clock is set back** (#6273, thanks @Afloat16). Before, cleanup could delete the snapshot it had just reported as saved.
- **`teambrain join` turns on the new sync connection even when the optional sharing step fails** (#6275, thanks @Afloat16).
- **Summaries with no progress in them are not stored** (#6202, thanks @ShitK). A summary with only a title or future plans used to be saved and announced as a success.
- **Claude Code's automatic messages no longer split a request** (#6251, thanks @Afloat16). The advisor and deliverable scans treated them as new requests and lost earlier advice and file writes from the same turn.
- **Corpus builds over 250,000 observations work** (#6271, thanks @Afloat16). They failed with `too many SQL variables`.
- **Codex: a plugin turned off with a dotted TOML key stays off** (#6239, thanks @Afloat16), for example `plugins."claude-mem@claude-mem-local".enabled = false`.
- **The mem-search skill's frontmatter is valid YAML** (#6276, thanks @Afloat16; reported in #6267 by @orbiutyt).
- **Aider:** the installer edits the config file Aider actually uses (working directory first, then git root, then home) (#6289, from #6230 by @Afloat16), and keeps quoted file paths intact in `read:` lists (#6290, from #6231 by @Afloat16).
- **Cursor and Grok context files keep the newer context** when two refreshes overlap (#6291, from #6232 by @Afloat16).
- **Self-hosted server:** a job with a revoked key or a scope violation runs once instead of three times (#6252), and `claude-mem server jobs retry` republishes with the queue's retries and backoff (#6253), thanks @HEOJUNFO. The OpenRouter provider reads at most 64 KiB when it checks an answer for a token-field error (#6238, thanks @Afloat16). One unreadable agent event no longer breaks every read of that table (#6199, thanks @DeryFerd).

## Security

- **shell-quote 1.11.0** (#6205, thanks @manippoudel; reported in #6200 by @lucasbritolubro). Version 1.9.0 is in the range of CVE-2026-102422 (critical). No code path in claude-mem reached the affected code; this takes it out of what ships.
- **adm-zip 0.6.1 and zod 4.6.7** in the plugin runtime, out of their High advisories (#6220, thanks @LeviReisJs; reported in #6211 by @noumanbhatti).
- **The Gemini API key goes in a header, not the request URL** (#6196, thanks @DeryFerd), so proxies and access logs don't record it.
- **Temp files get a random name and are created exclusively** at the remaining atomic-write sites (#6198, #6193, thanks @DeryFerd), so a planted symlink can't redirect a write of settings or state files.
- **The self-hosted server's unauthenticated `/v1/info` shows state only** (#6195, thanks @DeryFerd): no auth mode, schema version, Redis host or driver error text.
- CI: the postinstall allowlist check inspects every direct plugin dependency (#6197), and the spawn environment check reads env blocks declared above a spawn and scans the plugin runtime (#6194), thanks @DeryFerd.

## For contributors

- TypeScript 7.0.2 (#6207, thanks @krishnadobhal; #6188). The scripts and tests that use the compiler API keep TypeScript 6 through an alias.
- The import smoke test closes its SQLite readers before the final scan (#6216, thanks @liuyinchu).

name: v15.20.0
body:
## Two critical fixes

- **The worker starts when settings.json is not valid JSON** (#6259). The worker refused to start when `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` couldn't be parsed, even though the database already held the device identity it was trying to save there. Nothing was captured and no context was injected. It now logs a warning, leaves the file untouched, and starts. On a first start with no saved identity, the error names the file and says to repair or delete it.
- **Live Codex Desktop capture on macOS** (#6285, thanks @MaxWang007; reported in #6283 by @AlbertValverdeC). Under Bun on macOS, `fs.watch` gives no event while another process appends to a file it holds open, and Codex Desktop holds a rollout file open for the life of a thread. Codex sessions were read in one burst, sometimes a day later, when Codex closed the file. The transcript watcher now checks the files it already tails every 3 seconds and reads new bytes. It awaits one stat at a time, so a large `~/.codex/sessions` history never blocks the worker, and it never opens new files on its own.

## Also on main since 15.19.0

Three pieces of the upcoming 16.0.0, already on main, ship in this release too:

- **Mem0 and Supermemory import acceptance fixes** (#6206): Supermemory `--documents` reruns no longer duplicate, and documents imported by 15.19.0 still count as already imported. Mem0 expiry includes its own date. Every import limit names its source; the unsourced 100 MiB total and 10,000-record default are gone (`--max-records` stays).
- **Classic viewer and TV page redesign** (#6229): jumping to the end of a long timeline no longer crashes the viewer (React error 185). A one-row header, timeline kind chips with counts, "Find in loaded memories", day labels, session pages titled by their newest summary, tabbed Settings, and plainer logs. The TV page fits titles in up to three lines and shows a Live dot.
- **Setup step bar and Stop import** (#6233): a five-step bar with Back on every screen, errors in plain words with the raw cause under Details, and Stop import (`POST /api/setup/import/stop`, nothing deleted and nothing restarts by itself), with a receipt of what was added.

name: graphify 0.9.112
body:
- Docs: **python** the README, its translations, CONTRIBUTING, RELEASING, the bug-report template and the ruff/pyright targets now state Python 3.11 as the minimum, matching the floor that shipped in 0.9.111 (#5238, thanks @Deepanshu-Mehta; @Max17190 sent the same fix in #5237).
- Docs: **links** the Always-on setup link in the README and all translations points straight at docs.graphify.com/open-source/vibe-coding instead of going through a redirect from the old guides/always-on path (#5261, thanks @SyedFahad7).
- Fix: **java** each overloaded method gets its own node keyed by arity and erased signature, instead of all overloads collapsing into one node that dropped members and misrouted calls; `affected` override-matching is now arity-aware so a split `run(int)` is not tied to a supertype `run()` by label, and cross-repo and generic-method overloads are handled too (#5251, thanks @deba2k5). Same-arity, type-only-distinct overloads still bind to the first declared one (mirroring the C# precedent #4584); literal-argument-type dispatch is a follow-up. Overloaded constructors still share one node.
- Fix: **go** a bare receiver type (`func (s Service) m()`) resolves to its own package's type instead of being matched against every same-named type in the corpus, so two packages each declaring a `Service` keep their own member-call edges rather than both losing them to an ambiguity bail (#5242, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **rust** a `use crate::...` import resolves inside its own crate instead of leaking across crate boundaries to another crate's same-named item in a multi-crate workspace; a single-crate `crate::` import still resolves as before (#5240, thanks @Max17190).
- Fix: **js** a `this.x = function (params) {...}` member no longer fabricates a false `indirect_call` when one of its parameters shadows a same-named corpus function used in argument position; its own params and names captured from the enclosing scope are treated as local bindings, while a genuinely unbound name still resolves (#5241, thanks @Max17190).
- Fix: **c** a directory-qualified angle include (`#include <dir/header.h>`) resolves to the matching local file, and standard-library headers (`<stdio.h>`, `<functional>`) are kept off the alias index so a same-named project file is not healed onto them; a local header that shares a directory-qualified name still resolves (#5218, thanks @Yi-111-a).
- Fix: **sql** a table named with non-ASCII letters that the grammar collapses to a bare `_` no longer mints a node with an empty id or an edge to an empty id; the bogus edge is dropped instead (#5250, thanks @grbr2010).
- Fix: **dedup** a prefix-derived word is kept apart from its base word, so antonym and prefixed pairs (`synchronous`/`asynchronous`, `cyclic`/`acyclic`, `reload`/`load`) no longer fold together through the fuzzy label merge, while genuine inflections like `handler`/`handlers` still merge (#5239, thanks @Deepanshu-Mehta).
- Fix: **build** the cross-language edge guard's family table no longer drifts from the extractor's: 37 extensions that had no family entry (so a coincidental cross-language name collision was never dropped) are reconciled, and a test fails CI if the two tables diverge again (#5247, thanks @Yi-111-a).
- Fix: **install** `graphify claude install` writes its section to the file Claude Code actually reads. Claude Code reads a project's `AGENTS.md` only when no `CLAUDE.md` (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`) exists in the project or any directory above it, so creating a `CLAUDE.md` beside an `AGENTS.md` silently hid that `AGENTS.md` from Claude Code. The install now targets an existing `CLAUDE.md`/`.claude/CLAUDE.md` if present, else an existing `AGENTS.md`/`.claude/AGENTS.md`, else a new `CLAUDE.md` as before; uninstall is symmetric (#5277, thanks @andrebrait).
- Fix: **install** `graphify install` refuses to overwrite an existing Kilo config it cannot parse, instead of silently replacing it with a graphify-only file and losing the user's settings; a valid or missing config still merges as before (#5265, thanks @divya0795).
- Fix: **analyze** two-file import cycles are listed before the enumeration cap fills, so on a graph with many longer cycles the tightest (mutual two-file) cycles are no longer dropped; the listing is also now deterministic across runs (#5267, thanks @divya0795).
- Fix: **extract** the net-shrink guard is not armed for a source that has nothing to protect (one that never produced any saved nodes, e.g. a file whose optional grammar extra is not installed), so such a source no longer blocks a later extract that legitimately shrinks the graph; a source that did have saved records still arms the guard (#5245, thanks @ayushcodes10).
- Fix: **build** folding a Markdown document twin preserves the survivor's structure: a real heading node is no longer mistaken for the page's semantic twin and the page node (with its frontmatter and `contains` edges) is kept, while genuine semantic twins still fold (#5272, thanks @sdivyanshu90).
- Fix: **build** symlinked corpus aliases are pruned independently: excluding or deleting one symlink alias no longer also drops its target or a sibling alias that resolves to the same file, because prune matching now keys on the corpus path rather than the resolved physical target (#5273, thanks @sdivyanshu90).
- Fix: **pascal** a unit the tree-sitter grammar cannot parse end to end (for example one with an escaped SQL string literal) is recovered through a byte-length-preserving masked retry, instead of yielding no nodes; the retry runs only when the normal parse errored and is accepted only if strictly healthier, so units that already parse are unchanged (#5264, thanks @patrykseksymfonia).
- Fix: **pascal** a base class resolves to its real declaration in the unit it is declared in, instead of a stub matched by filename convention, so the `inherits` edge and the inherited calls through it resolve across files (#5280, thanks @patrykseksymfonia).
- Fix: **pascal** a call through a global object variable (`DM.Open`, the Delphi data-module idiom) resolves to the variable's type member: the extractor records unit-level globals, per-class fields and per-routine shadows, and resolution binds the qualified call fail-closed through the uses-clause, leaving it unresolved when a field, local or array-typed global shadows the name (#3101, thanks @patrykseksymfonia).
- Feat: **delphi** a form (`.dfm`/`.lfm`) is linked to the unit that implements it: the form class and each `OnClick = Handler` stub get an INFERRED `references` edge to the real class and method in the sibling `.pas`, paired by base name and a unique class/method lookup (#5281, thanks @patrykseksymfonia).

The AST cache schema is bumped to 48; warm caches re-run the affected Go, Java, JS/TS, C/C++, SQL and Pascal extractions.

## [2.10.6] ### Bug Fixes - [`27f96ecba`](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/commit/27f96ecba7ce5c913115ea38daeba02fe77cf35e) ([#16564](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/16564) by [@nickrmurphy](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/../../nickrmurphy)) Fix the macOS bundle failing under the Node CLI with `failed to run actool` (`Bad file descriptor` or an `NSPlaceholderArray` exception, depending on the Xcode version) when `bundle > icon` includes an Icon Composer `.icon` file, by running `actool` with a null stdin. - [`371882e0f`](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/commit/371882e0f51dc01e9ef31c3a746d89c09c333ea2) ([#16555](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/pull/16555) by [@rawsun007](https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/../../rawsun007)) Name the `customLanguageFiles` NSIS config key in the warning for untranslated languages, instead of `custom_language_files`, which the config rejects. ### Dependencies - Upgraded to `tauri-utils@2.10.4`

name: v2.2.1
body:
### Fixes
- fix: omp read with a line range in the path is a bounded read, not replaced (#1392)
- fix: recall skips rows and line units written after the latest compaction (#1394)
- fix: SessionStart(compact) sends the state block once per compaction, not once per session (#1396)
- fix: ctx_search names an unknown explicit source and the stored sources (#1390)
- fix: setup keeps a working OpenCode install when the host list command exits non-zero (#1386)
- fix: rtk proxy / bypass reads get the same Codex size check as the plain command (#1388)
- fix: Windows mkdir EPERM on the context.db publish claim waits like EEXIST (#1385, D-1385-NOLINK-2)
- fix: doctor lists a v1 data dir setup keeps as a note, not a FAIL (#1383)
- fix: subagent with no route to the stored output gets it whole; built-in claude gets ctx_search (#1382)
- fix: Pi >= 1.5 gets the payload as a named section, so <mcp_servers> stays (#1384)
- fix: publish a fresh context.db where link() is denied (EACCES/EPERM on Android f2fs) (#1385)

### Who gets this

One version on both channels: the release commit on main (GitHub) and npm.

| Agent | Channel | Update with |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | GitHub | `claude plugin update context-mode@context-mode` |
| Codex | GitHub, npm for the one-time hook trust step | `codex plugin marketplace upgrade context-mode` |
| Gemini CLI | GitHub | `gemini extensions update context-mode` |
| Qwen Code | GitHub | `qwen extensions update context-mode` |
| Copilot CLI | npm | `context-mode upgrade` |
| VS Code (Copilot) | npm | `context-mode upgrade` |
| Kiro | npm | `context-mode upgrade` |
| ZCode | GitHub | `zcode plugins update context-mode@context-mode` |
| Pi | npm | `pi update --extensions` |
| OpenCode | npm | `opencode plugin update` |
| OMP | npm | `omp plugin upgrade context-mode` |

body:
# Cua Driver 0.53.2

## Summary

This release includes 1 fix.

## Fixes

- add started_at_unix_ms to recording session.json. ([#8118](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8118)) Thanks @Iflaqbhat; reported by @methanoya.

## Contributors

Thanks to @Iflaqbhat, @methanoya for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.

body:
# Cua Driver 0.53.1

## Summary

This release includes 4 fixes.

## Fixes

- report macOS AX enumeration counts in ax_window_unresolved. ([#8096](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8096)) Thanks @lorenzozanee; reported by @JayLewisLLC.
- publish display-only rows as observations so verify_state can read them. ([#7566](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/7566))
- run a background pixel-targeted menu key equivalent on macOS. ([#8081](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8081)) reported by @howardxie-dev.
- explain session-scoped snapshots in the stale token error. ([#8110](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/8110)) Thanks @Alx8g.

## Contributors

Thanks to @Alx8g, @howardxie-dev, @JayLewisLLC, @lorenzozanee for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.
